You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

Abdul earns $50000 a year working as a teacher. He owns a house valued at $250000 and has shares worth $20000. He has a current bank account with a balance of $1500 and $200 in his wallet. In his house there is a jar containing $100, which he has saved to spend on his forthcoming holiday. What is the value of Abdul’s liquid assets?
Which type of good is healthcare?

options.B: free
options.C: merit
options.D: public

questions.questionText: Which is a normative statement?

options.A: If interest rates fall consumption is likely to increase.
options.B: If interest rates fall consumption will definitely increase.
options.C: Interest rates and consumption are usually inversely related.
options.D: The rate of interest should be reduced.

questions.questionText: In a free market there is a surplus of a good. Which change would cause the market to come to an equilibrium?

options.B: a fall in price
options.C: a government minimum price
options.D: an increase in supply

questions.questionText: What is most likely to increase the quantity of houses supplied?

options.A: a policy to help house buyers on modest incomes
options.B: a restriction on the level of rent that can be charged
options.C: a rise in the tax on materials used for building houses
options.D: the removal of a subsidy to house builders

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two demand curves and two supply curves for a product. Which equilibrium point is most likely to represent the long-run equilibrium in the market? S S price A B D

options.C: D D O quantity

questions.questionText: The equilibrium price of a product is $10. The government introduces an effective minimum price of $12 for the product. Under which condition will the value of the producer surplus increase the most? price elasticity of demand

options.B: between 0 and 1
options.D: greater than 1

questions.questionText: Diesel engines are a major cause of air pollution in cities. A city authority placed a charge on diesel taxis entering the city. What would be the most likely effects on the demand and supply of taxi journeys into the city? demand for supply of taxi journeys taxi journeys

options.B: fall remain unchanged
options.C: remain unchanged fall
options.D: rise fall

questions.questionText: Which combination of the classification of a good and market change will cause the demand curve for the good to shift right? classification of good market change

options.B: inferior good price decrease
options.C: normal good income decrease
options.D: normal good price decrease

questions.questionText: The supply (S) of a product is determined by the equation S = 10 + 10P when P is the price of the product in $. What is the product’s price elasticity of supply when its price rises from $1 to $2?

The table gives estimates of the price elasticities and cross elasticities of demand for bus and rail travel. elasticity with respect to the price of service bus travel rail travel bus travel –0.37 +0.13 rail travel +0.16 –0.43 What would be the change in the volume of rail travel resulting from a 1% increase in bus fares?

options.B: a decrease of 0.37%
options.C: an increase of 0.16%
options.D: an increase of 0.43%

questions.questionText: Which combination is most likely to result in the demand for a product being highly price-elastic? number of close % of income substitutes spent on product

options.B: large small
options.C: small large
options.D: small small

questions.questionText: What is most likely to occur when the government privatises public sector organisations?

options.B: Employment will increase in the short run.
options.C: Innovation will be discouraged.
options.D: The production of public goods will increase.

The diagram shows the market for eye tests. price of eye S tests ($) P P P D O Q Q

In November 2017, the Scottish government introduced a minimum price for alcohol because of the detrimental health effects of alcohol consumption. Which combination of actions is most likely to lead to a failure with respect to reducing the detrimental effects of the consumption of alcohol? action 1 action 2

options.A: minimum price is set too high effective information provision regarding the health effects of consuming alcohol
options.B: minimum price is set too high effective subsidisation of non-alcoholic beverages
options.C: minimum price is set too low health benefits of reduced alcohol consumption have been overestimated
options.D: minimum price is set too low stricter enforcement of the regulations relating to the sale of alcohol

questions.questionText: What is an example of direct provision by a government?

options.A: The government introduces a subsidy on renewable fuels to help the environment.
options.B: The government introduces a unit tax on cigarettes to discourage consumption.
options.C: The government sets a maximum rent on housing to protect tenants.
options.D: The government takes over a private library to improve local services.

questions.questionText: The graph shows the annual percentage change in the prices of services and in the prices of goods between 2007 and 2012. % annual 8 price change 6 services 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 –2 goods –4 What can be deduced from the graph?

options.A: On average the price of services was higher than the price of goods throughout the period.
options.B: The average price of goods was higher in 2012 than in 2010.
options.C: The average price of services was higher in 2012 than in 2010.
options.D: There was a fall in the general price level between 2008 and 2010.

questions.questionText: A government decides to devalue the country’s currency to remove the deficit on its current account of the balance of payments. What is the most likely reason why this would not work?

options.A: The country gains a competitive advantage from the devaluation.
options.B: The country has a surplus on its capital and financial accounts.
options.C: The price elasticities of demand for the country’s exports and imports are greater than one.
options.D: There are high trade barriers with the country’s main trading partners.

questions.questionText: What will increase if aggregate demand rises when aggregate supply is perfectly elastic?

options.B: real output
options.C: the price level
options.D: wage rates

questions.questionText: A country operates a floating exchange rate. What will cause the demand curve for the country’s currency to shift left in the foreign exchange market?

options.A: a decrease in the country’s interest rate
options.B: a decrease in the country’s money supply
options.C: an increase in the country’s export sales
options.D: an increase in the country’s import purchases

questions.questionText: The table shows the relative price of exports compared with imports expressed as an index number for an economy (2013 = 100). date index 2013 100 2014 97 2015 95 Which statement about the period 2013–2015 is correct?

options.A: Export prices have increased each year.
options.B: The general level of prices has fallen.
options.C: The terms of trade have deteriorated.
options.D: The volume of imports increasingly exceeds the volume of exports.

questions.questionText: The table shows an extract from a country’s balance of payments. exports imports $ billion $ billion trade in goods 150 200 trade in services 70 50 primary (investment) income 120 100 secondary (transfer) income 15 20 What is the current account balance?
The real national income of a country fell by 3%. What could have caused this?

options.A: Money national income fell by 3% when the rate of inflation was 6%.
options.B: Money national income fell by 6% when the rate of inflation was 3%.
options.C: Money national income rose by 3% when the rate of inflation was 6%.
options.D: Money national income rose by 6% when the rate of inflation was 3%.

questions.questionText: An economy with a long history of extensive barriers to trade decides to switch to totally free trade. What is most likely to increase in the short term?

options.B: government revenue
options.C: inflationary pressure
options.D: profits of all domestic companies

questions.questionText: Why is a balance of payments deficit a potential problem for an economy with a fixed exchange rate?

options.B: Rival economies may react with trade protection measures.
options.C: The economy’s foreign exchange reserves may decrease.
options.D: The economy’s short-run standard of living will be reduced.

questions.questionText: What would be a positive effect on the growth of an economy in the short run, if the government reduced a direct tax on individual earnings?

options.A: food prices would increase due to shortages
options.B: imports of luxury cars would increase to satisfy a change in demand
options.C: savings would increase due to additional disposable income
options.D: the consumption of domestically produced goods would increase

questions.questionText: Which combination of fiscal and monetary policies is most likely to be effective in the short run for tackling deflation in a closed economy? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: decreasing the budget deficit decreasing the interest rate
options.B: decreasing the budget deficit decreasing the money supply
options.C: increasing the budget deficit decreasing the interest rate
options.D: increasing the budget deficit decreasing the money supply

questions.questionText: Which policy measure is an expenditure-switching measure designed to reduce a current account surplus?

options.A: a cut in income tax rates
options.B: a depreciation of the exchange rate
options.C: the removal of limits on bank lending
